claims.claim: On Wednesday, a New Mexico court ordered Meta, the parent of Facebook, to pay a $25 billion penalty for misleading consumers about data privacy.
claims.bestSource: Cambridge Analytica: Meta Hit With Record $25 Billion Penalty in New Mexico - www.trendingtopics.eu
claims.evidence: Meta was ordered to pay $25 billion in penalties by a New Mexico court on Wednesday as part of a data privacy case that stemmed from the company's Cambridge Analytica scandal from nearly a decade ago. A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion after a jury found the company guilty of misleading consumers about the privacy of their data a decade ago. Eight years on, Cambridge Analytica is costing Meta more than any settlement: A court in the U.S. state of New Mexico has just ordered the Facebook parent to pay a penalty of $25 billion.

The New Mexico penalty is five times as large. Torrez sees it as a warning to the entire tech industry, explicitly including social media and A.I. companies. At the heart of the case is the Cambridge Analytica scandal. New Mexico sued in 2021, accusing Facebook of misleading users for years about how it handled their data. Statements about its handling of misinformation and hate speech were also part of the lawsuit. Prosecutors said the company made 26 misleading statements about data privacy over 11 years. New Mexico deliberately chose not to join the joint settlement and took its claims to trial instead. According to New York Attorney General Letitia James , who led a coalition of 51 attorneys general in total, Meta will pay at least $12.1 billion and up to $17.1 billion.
